title: Degree-zero cochains are invariants
statement: Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, $A$ a finite ring, and $\mathcal C$ the abelian category of left $A$-modules with $A$-linear $G$-action and open stabilizers [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(A\text{-Mod},\mathbb N)$ have termwise linear equivalences $F(M)^n\simeq\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)$, natural by postcomposition, and differentials $d^0m(g)=gm-m$ and $d^nf(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^jf(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$. There exists an additive functor $V:\mathcal C\to A\text{-Mod}$ preserving finite limits, with natural linear equivalences $V(M)\simeq\bigcap_{g\in G}\ker(\rho_M(g)-1)$ whose maps are restrictions of the coefficient maps. The degree-zero homology functor of $F$ is naturally isomorphic to $V$.

proof.text: Define V(M) as the intersection of kernels of rho(g)-id. Restrict an equivariant map to this submodule. Identities, composition and addition hold pointwise. This is an explicit construction rather than choice of an arbitrary witness.

Identify the continuous maps from G^0, a singleton, with the coefficient module by evaluation. The displayed degree-zero differential vanishes precisely on the invariant submodule. Degree-zero cohomology has no incoming boundaries, hence equals this kernel; the evaluation identifications commute with every coefficient map and give a natural isomorphism. Kernels and finite products of representations are computed on underlying modules. Invariant elements commute with both these constructions, so V preserves finite limits.
